state.case_summary:
A patient in their 80s presented with dyspnea and syncope during exercise. Medical history included essential hypertension and Parkinson disease. The patient reported experiencing dyspnea on exertion and exercise intolerance for the past year, with difficulty walking more than 100m. They also experienced syncope during a bicycle ride with loss of consciousness for a few minutes, followed by complete recovery.

Vital signs were normal except for elevated blood pressure of 150/78 mm Hg. Chest auscultation revealed normal breath and heart sounds without any murmurs.

- Laboratory tests: Hemogram, serum electrolytes, and thyroid function test were within normal limits.- Echocardiogram findings:  - Normal left ventricular ejection fraction (74%)  - Normal wall motion  - Left atrial enlargement (volume index, 34.89 mL/m2)  - Uncertain diastolic function  - No significant valvular abnormality  - Pulmonary hypertension (mean pulmonary arterial pressure 32 mm Hg)- ECG findings:  Image Title: Initial ECG  Image Description: Shows sinus rhythm with first-degree atrioventricular block (PR interval 360 ms), right bundle-branch block (RBBB) and left anterior fascicular block (LAFB). Wide QRS complex (120 ms), rSR in lead V1, and RS in lead V6 (deep and wide S waves ≥40 ms). Left axis deviation and qR in leads I and aVL, and rS in leads II, III, and aVF.- 24-hour ECG monitoring:  Image Title: Continuous ambulatory ECG monitoring  Image Description: Shows sinus rhythm (average 60 beats/min), PR prolongation (360 ms) and third-degree AV block with minimum heart rate of 36 beats/min. Mobitz type I second-degree AV block with pause and junctional escape beat observed. No atrial/ventricular arrhythmia found.
